title: Evaluating Expressions and Formulas
short: Substitute numbers for variables and simplify.
trouble: Students read 3x with x = 4 as 34 instead of 3 × 4.

blocks.html: To evaluate an expression, put in a number for each variable you wrote and work it out with the order of operations.
Substitute: replace each variable with its value, in parentheses if that helps. Then simplify in the usual order. $3x + 5$ when $x = 4$ is $3(4) + 5 = 17$.

A variable stands for a number. Once you know the number, the expression is an ordinary numerical expression, so all the rules you already know apply. Writing the value in parentheses keeps the operations visible: $3x$ with $x = 4$ becomes $3(4)$, which means $3 \times 4$, not the number 34.

head: $x$
blocks.cap: One expression, many values: as $x$ changes, so does $3x + 5$.

blocks.title: A formula
blocks.q: The perimeter of a rectangle is $P = 2\ell + 2w$. Find $P$ when $\ell = 8$ cm and $w = 3.5$ cm.

blocks.title: An exponent in a formula
blocks.q: The surface area of a cube is $A = 6s^2$. Find $A$ when $s = 3$.

blocks.html: Gluing the digits together: reading $3x$ with $x = 4$ as 34. A number next to a variable always means multiply. Quick check: write the value in parentheses, $3(4)$, before you compute.
